name: Extramammary Paget Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Extramammary Paget Disease

criteria.description: Presence of Paget cells with abundant pale cytoplasm and prominent nuclei in the epidermis
Positive staining for cytokeratin 7 (CK7) and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA)
Chronic, well-demarcated erythematous, eczematous or scaly plaques in apocrine gland-rich areas

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological identification of Paget cells plus positive immunohistochemical markers (CK7 and CEA) in characteristic clinical lesions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from melanoma and other intraepithelial neoplasms is critical.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Well-demarcated erythematous plaque with eczematous changes
searchTerms: red, well-defined skin patch with eczema

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of Paget cells in epidermis confirmed by biopsy
searchTerms: cancer cells in skin confirmed by biopsy
presence of abnormal Paget cells in epidermis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chronic pruritus localized to apocrine gland-rich areas
searchTerms: chronic itching in sweat gland areas
persistent itch in apocrine gland regions

common.symptomName: Erosions or ulcerations within the lesion
searchTerms: skin breaks or ulcers in lesion

common.symptomName: Scaling and crusting of affected skin

searchTerms: hot or painful feeling on skin

rare.symptomName: Urinary or gastrointestinal symptoms due to underlying malignancy
searchTerms: bladder or bowel issues from cancer

laboratory: Histopathology showing Paget cells with large pale cytoplasm and prominent nuclei
Immunohistochemical positivity for CK7, CEA, and EMA
Negative staining for S100 and HMB-45 to exclude melanoma
imaging: Ultrasound or CT scan for regional lymph node assessment
MRI or PET scan to evaluate for underlying or invasive malignancy
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic erythematous plaques in apocrine gland-rich areas (e.g., vulva, perianal region, scrotum)

distinguishingFeatures: Involvement of nipple-areolar complex rather than extramammary sites
Positive immunohistochemical staining for S100 and HMB-45
Presence of atypical melanocytes rather than Paget cells
Absence of Paget cells on biopsy
Clinical history of chronic rubbing or scratching
Histopathology shows epidermal hyperplasia without neoplastic cells

redFlags: Failure to respond to topical corticosteroids or antifungal treatments
references: Hatta N, et al. Extramammary Paget's Disease: Clinicopathological Features and Treatment. J Dermatol. 2020;47(6):595-602.
Kanitakis J. Mammary and extramammary Paget's disease. J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol. 2007;21(5):581-90.
